statement: For Lambda_L={1,...,L-1}^4 with the Dirichlet nearest-neighbor graph Laplacian h_L of edge weight J, K_L=dGamma(h_L^2/128), beta=tau L^4, and H_0=K_L-lambda M/L^4 for fixed J,tau>0 and lambda in a compact subset of (-infinity,0], every nonnegative closed quadratic form W with D(q_0) intersect D(w) dense, q_0+w closed, and W vanishing on the no-double-occupancy subspace satisfies D(rho_W||rho_0)=O((log L)^(-1/2)) and ||rho_W-rho_0||_1=O((log L)^(-1/4)), uniformly in W. W may mix number sectors. The same conclusion holds for hard compression onto a closed allowed subspace containing no-double occupancy when the restricted free form is densely defined.
supplied_inputs: Finite 4D box and Dirichlet nearest-neighbor Laplacian with edge weight J
Fixed tau,J>0 and compact nonpositive lambda interval
Closed nonnegative W form with the exact domain and null-subspace assumptions in the statement
costs: No numerical computation, interacting spectrum, Gibbs oracle, or acquired input. Constants are convergent free-mode sums depending on J,tau and the compact lambda interval. Spatial size S=(L-1)^4; filter radius ell=floor(sqrt L). No bit-complexity or state-preparation guarantee. Asymptotic KL rate O((log L)^(-1/2)); full trace-norm rate O((log L)^(-1/4)).
matched_baseline: The free Gibbs state rho_0 at the same finite-volume dispersion, beta, scaled chemical parameter, and full Fock space.
strongest_control: The comparison holds uniformly over all nonnegative closed forms satisfying the null-subspace and form-sum assumptions, including fixed-strength local positive penalties that vanish on no-double occupancy, hard exclusion, and number-mixing forms.
falsifier_or_failure_mode: A failure of the exact zero-extension commutator, the C^2 discrete A_2 bound, the symmetric-Fock derivative-pair normalization, fixed-tilt absorption, or the W-null-on-ran-F domain condition would invalidate the proof. These interfaces were checked in AUDIT_RECEIPT.txt under the stated graph convention; no counterexample was found.

primary_source_baseline.reference: Jianda Wu, Fei Zhou, Congjun Wu, Quantum criticality of bosonic systems with the Lifshitz dispersion
primary_source_baseline.relevance: Qualitative Lifshitz phi^4 upper-critical-dimension context; it does not prove this lattice whole-Fock Gibbs relative-entropy theorem.
